_doc: NUTRITION. Every creature (enemies.json 'nutrition') and forage food (events.json forage.<id>.nutrition) has a profile of nutrient points. Each meal is rated against the species diet weights: Great / Okay / Poor / Harmful ('fit_labels', per-meal score = sum(weight*nutrient)). DIET QUALITY is a ROLLING score over your last 'rolling.window' meals (recent meals weigh more; empty slots count 0; monoculture is penalised; harmful or junk meals subtract), so eating everything gives a mediocre diet - only selective eating earns the growth bonus and unlocks branches. Eating modes (per kill): 'Eat' = savour it (nutrients + rating count, but only eat_hunger_mult of its hunger) or 'Just fill up' = full hunger, no nutrients, logged as junk (fill_pts). There are NO stat penalties for a poor diet: it only keeps stronger evolution branches LOCKED. requires: nutrient minimums (lifetime meters), 'max_toxin', 'diet_score'.

carnivore.desc: Thrives on meat: protein, fat and minerals. Plant matter does nothing for you; toxins undo good meals.

_doc_xp: Growth bonus: XP from every fight is multiplied by 1 + xp_bonus[diet quality] (modest, +0..25%). Poor eating never reduces XP below normal.

meal_mult._doc: Per meal-fit label: heal = food/4 x heal, and the nutrients that go into your meters x nutrients. Great meals are worth more; junk is mostly empty calories, so eating everything buys survival but not growth.
